name: Jordan
summary: Created as the British mandate of Transjordan in 1921 under the Hashemite family; independent in 1946; a stable kingdom that hosts many refugees.

location.value: East of the Jordan River; about 89,000 km².

climate.value: Mostly hot, dry desert; the western highlands have a Mediterranean climate with winter rain and sometimes snow.

resources.value: Phosphate, and potash from the Dead Sea, but very little water and no large oil reserves.

disasters.value: Droughts and severe water shortage, flash floods such as those near the Dead Sea in 2018, and occasional earthquakes.

population.value: About 11 million people (2024), including many refugees and foreign workers.

urbanisation.value: Over 90% urban; the Amman area holds about 4 million people, followed by Zarqa and Irbid.

disease.value: Good health care by regional standards; water shortage and crowded refugee camps create health risks.

migration.value: Palestinian refugees arrived in 1948 and 1967, Iraqis after 2003, and over 600,000 registered Syrian refugees after 2011.

economicBase.value: Services, tourism (such as Petra), phosphate and potash mining, money sent home by workers abroad, and foreign aid.

tradeRoutes.value: Aqaba on the Red Sea is the only port; highways link Jordan to Iraq, Saudi Arabia and Syria.

wealth.value: A middle-income country with few natural resources, high unemployment and a reliance on foreign aid.

moneyAndTax.value: The Jordanian dinar, introduced in 1950 and pegged to the US dollar since 1995.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A constitutional monarchy under the 1952 constitution, in which the king holds wide powers alongside an elected parliament.

keyRulers.value: King Abdullah I (1946–51), the founder; King Hussein (1952–99), who ruled for nearly 47 years; his son became king in 1999.

succession.value: Hereditary in the Hashemite family; the king names the crown prince from among his sons or brothers.

institutions.value: A parliament with an elected House of Representatives and a Senate appointed by the king, and a prime minister chosen by the king.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: Arab Legion, now the Jordan Armed Forces.

majorWars.value: The Arab–Israeli wars of 1948 and 1967, when Jordan lost the West Bank, and the Black September conflict of 1970–71.

territoryChange.value: Held the West Bank and East Jerusalem from 1948 (annexed 1950) until 1967; gave up its claim in 1988.

alliancesRivals.value: Close to Britain and the US; peace treaty with Israel (1994).

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: High literacy (over 95% of adults); the University of Jordan in Amman was founded in 1962.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: The Desert Highway and King’s Highway run north–south, the old Hejaz Railway passes through Amman, and Queen Alia Airport serves the capital.

languageWriting.value: Arabic is the official language; English is widely used in business and education.

artsArchitecture.value: Ancient sites such as Nabataean Petra and Roman Jerash, and the white stone buildings of modern Amman.

socialStructure.value: Jordanians of East Bank and Palestinian origin.

sharedIdentity.value: Loyalty to the Hashemite monarchy and Arab identity, with debates over East Bank and Palestinian-origin identities.

dailyLife.value: Most people live in city apartments; mansaf (lamb with rice and yogurt) is the national dish, and coffee marks hospitality.

neighbours.value: Syria, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Israel and the West Bank, with a short Red Sea coast at Aqaba.

ideasReligions.value: Sunni Islam with a moderate official tone; the Hashemite kings claim descent from the Prophet Muhammad and act as custodians of Jerusalem’s holy sites.

riseSignals.value: Independence as the Hashemite Kingdom of Transjordan on 25 May 1946; renamed Jordan in 1949.

peakPeriod.value: Too recent to judge; it has stayed stable while several neighbours faced wars.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Still in existence as a Hashemite kingdom with its capital at Amman.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
